This PDF is only 1 page with no prose restatement duplicating any inline numbers (single-mention style throughout, Style B per description-format.md) — nothing looked garbled from PDF extraction, but there was also no second copy of any number (e.g. Burning Strike's '3d10' and jjScale '10d10' max) to cross-validate against.

Every técnica/manifestação in this hatsu ties its numeric outcome to a raw dice roll (1d20, 1d8, d100) multiplied by a fixed factor (x5, x7, x8h) or split by parity (odd/even), rather than the system's usual attack-roll-hits-then-roll-damage-dice pattern. None of these are 'damage die is d10/d12 gated by an attack roll' in the documented sense, so I did NOT build attack/save/heal/damage Activities for any of them — everything is modeled as type:'utility' with the full mechanic left as description text, per the skill's guidance to fall back to text when the mechanic doesn't map cleanly to a native Activity field. This is a deliberate, hatsu-wide call, not an oversight — please sanity check given how unusual this hatsu is.

Love Punch: attack roll determines hit, then 1d20 rolled and split by parity into either healing (half the roll x5) or bludgeoning damage (roll x5) — this is a coin-flip/parity-branch that dnd5e's heal/attack/damage Activity shapes can't represent as a single Activity (can't conditionally be heal OR damage from one roll). Left as utility + full text; flag if a two-activity 'Comum/heal vs damage' split is wanted instead.

Flag if you'd prefer an actual damage Activity (1d8, bludgeoning, no attack/save) instead.

This whole hatsu is essentially 'mechanically freeform, described entirely in prose' by nature of its design (coin flips, parity branches, percentile multipliers, max-HP-loss-until-rest) and none of it fits the documented jjScale/attack/save/heal shapes.
